newsitem.title: USA: Iowa, Virginia governors seek UPS intervention.
newsitem.headline: Iowa, Virginia governors seek UPS intervention.

text.p: The governors of Iowa and Virginia have written to President Clinton asking him to intervene in the Teamsters union strike against United Parcel Service, now in its fifth day.
Clinton told a news conference this week that there would have to be "severe damage" to the economy before he would be justified in intervening in the strike under federal law.
Gov. Terry Branstad of Iowa said he was particularly concerned about the impact the strike was having on the delivery of medical supplies.

"My office has also received numerous calls from small businesses whose livelihoods rely heavily on prompt deliveries from the United Parcel Service," Branstad also said in his letter, which was dated Aug. 7 and released here Friday.
Gov. George Allen of Virginia said many of the jobs created in Virginia recently had been at mail order companies.
"Without rapid resolution to this strike, thousands of Virginians will have to be laid off because they are unable to process their orders from customers," Allen wrote on Aug. 5.
Allen said he believed the challenges posed by the UPS strike were equal to those of the American Airlines' pilots dispute, which Clinton intervened in earlier this year.
Talks between UPS and the union under the guidance of federal mediators were due to resume in Washington at noon EDT (1600 GMT).
